name: Basilica of St. Hyacinth
history: Resurrectionist priests from Chicago's first Polish parish founded St. Hyacinth in 1894. Money and construction problems delayed the present church for years; the first Mass in it was on 7 August 1921 and it was dedicated that October. It became a basilica in 2003, one of three in the Archdiocese of Chicago.
arch: A red-brick Classical Revival church in the "Polish Cathedral" style, with a Baroque-influenced interior. Its three-towered front is rare in American church architecture.
features: Its bells, from the McShane Bell Foundry of Baltimore, were blessed and hung in 1924.
A restoration from the mid-1990s took almost a decade, with murals by Conrad Schmitt Studios.

look.d: A three-towered facade is rare in American churches.
The clock and towers rise over Chicago's Avondale neighborhood.

fun: St. Wenceslaus parish was founded in 1912 just to relieve the crowds at St. Hyacinth.
journal: Three towers of red brick and terra cotta: Polish Chicago building big.
